title: Claims Review Board Ruling: Claim History and Undelivered-Parcel Delivery Refunds
content:
Claims Review Board ruling for Delivery Claims: on a Delivered Not Received or Lost in Transit Claim, the delivery-charge refund reflects the delivery-claim refunds the customer has received on other orders over the past year.

**Ruling.** The claim-history share depends on the refunds with reason delivery claim (of merchandise or of a delivery charge) paid on the customer's other orders in the trailing 12 calendar months, as they stand on the orders' payment records, each refund entry counted once: four or more pay 50% of the basis, two or three pay 75%, and one or none leave the basis whole.

## What is counted

- Order-level refund entries on the payment records of the customer's orders other than the order of this claim.
- Whose reason is delivery claim — whether the refund was of merchandise (booked against an order line) or of a delivery charge.
- Dated in the 12 calendar months up to today.
- Each refund entry once.

| Delivery-claim refund entries on other orders, trailing 12 months | Claim-history share |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 100% — the basis whole |
| 2 or 3 | 75% |
| 4 or more | 50% |

## Cases (hypothetical payment records)

- Three delivery-claim refund entries on two other orders this year, plus one on the order of this claim: the entry on this claim's order is not counted; 3 entries — 75%.
- Four delivery-claim refund entries on other orders, one of them dated 15 months ago: 3 fall in the window — 75%.
- One merchandise refund and one delivery-charge refund, both with reason delivery claim, on another order in the window: 2 entries — 75%.
- A return refund on another order: its reason is not delivery claim — not counted.
